title: Checkmate and stalemate
line: Check with no way out wins. No legal move and no check is a draw.

steps.text: This is checkmate: the king is in check, and no move gets it out. Here Black has won in two moves.
Checkmate the black king with your rook in one move.
steps.hint: Your king already covers the squares in front of the black king.
steps.after: Checkmate. The rook checks, and your king covers every escape.

steps.text: This is stalemate: Black is to move and not in check, but has no move the rules allow. The game is a draw: nobody wins.
Checkmate in one with the queen. Careful: two queen moves leave Black no move and no check.

wrong.b1b6: That is stalemate: Black has no move the rules allow and is not in check. The game is a draw.
wrong.b1g1: That is stalemate: Black has no move the rules allow and is not in check. The game is a draw.

steps.hint: Check the king where your king guards the queen, or along the edge of the board.

steps.text: Stalemate is a draw even when one side is far ahead. With more pieces, always leave the other king a move until you can mate.

summary: Checkmate is check with no way out, and it wins. No move at all, and no check, is stalemate: a draw.
